messages:
Ryan: alert-bot flagged a sudden spike in 5xx (503/500) across hosted inference API in us-west-2. Customer impact reported. Alert shows upstream worker failures, not gateway timeouts. Pods are restarting.

Aisha: saw the dashboard — 3.2% error rate, P95 latency up ~2x. Which service/pool is affected?

Dom: inference-deploy-rlhf-*-pods. `kubectl get pods -n hosted | grep inference | grep CrashLoop` shows 4/12 with restarts.

Leah: grabbing logs from one of the failing pods, paste below:

```
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] runtime error: segfault at 0x0
GPU failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes: out of memory
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
stack trace:
  inference::kv_cache::evict+0x2f
  inference::kernel_select::apply+0x14b
```

Aisha: that looks like a GPU OOM followed by a native segfault. Was there a recent change?

Dom: yes — we rolled a canary of the continuous-batching + kernel-optimizations patch at 10:05 UTC (10% traffic), ramped to 50% around 10:10. Spike started ~10:11. deploy-bot logs show the rollout.

Ryan: confirmed via deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: rollout inference-runtime v2.13 -> v2.14 (continuous-batching enabled) at 10:04 UTC`

Leah: flamegraphs show kv-cache size growing linearly for some requests where sequence length hit ~9k tokens (long chat sessions). Memory footprint blew past expected allocation and allocation failed.

Aisha: Support found a repro from a customer. Sample request that reproduces OOM on canary node:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-v2","prompt":"<long chat>","max_tokens":6000,"stream":false}'
```

Dom: running that against a canary pod locally reproduces OOM and segfault ~20s in. Confirmed.

Ryan: immediate mitigation plan: rollback the canary to previous batcher, cordon the failing nodes, scale up the pool by +4 GPUs, and enable fallback to the quantized/CPU path for long-seq requests. Also notify CS.

Leah: initiated rollback: `deploy-bot: rollback inference-runtime-canary v2.14 -> v2.13` (reaction :white_check_mark:).

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 10:30 UTC.

Aisha: cordoned affected nodes with `kubectl cordon <node>` and drained failing pods. Increased node pool min from 12 -> 16 temporarily to absorb traffic.

Dom: added a temporary request-level guard: if max_tokens > 4000 OR seq_length_estimate > 5k then route to quantized-variant or reject with 413-like guidance (support message).

Ryan: customer comms draft: "We observed elevated 5xx errors for long-running chat sessions between 10:11–10:28 UTC due to upstream worker restarts during a canary rollout. We've rolled back the canary and restarted affected nodes. If you continue to see errors please reduce max_tokens or enable streaming; we're following up with a root-cause analysis."

Leah: root-cause hypothesis: interaction between continuous-batching change + kernel selection bug + unbounded kv-cache growth for extreme seq lengths -> GPU memory leak then segfault on allocation failure.

Aisha: follow-ups assigned: (1) revert continuous-batching default until ready, (2) add per-request kv-cache accounting + eviction, (3) add safe-fallback path when GPU memory low, (4) add a canary safety gate for long-seq traffic.

Dom: opened RED-INC-4821 with logs, repro steps, pod manifests, and dmesg output.

Ryan: tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for RCA, scheduled postmortem tomorrow. Notifying CS and account teams now.

Leah: CS template saved to incidents page for outreach.

Aisha: monitoring shows 5xx back to baseline ~10:42 UTC after rollback and scale-up. Keeping alert window open for 2h.

Ryan: thanks team — great triage. Will follow up with postmortem action items. :heart:
